n43b27cfa1ce.s:
Consider the following statements about ICAR's high-yielding varieties:
1. ICAR released 562 new high-yielding field-crop varieties during 2019-21.
2. More HYVs have been notified since 2014 than during the whole of 1969-2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n43b27cfa1ce.x: ICAR released 562 new HYVs in 2019-21. Statement 2 is wrong: 3,236 HYVs were notified since 2014 against 3,969 in 1969-2014.

n34dbd6d91f7.s: Besides HYV seeds, the Green Revolution package approach included:
o: Withdrawal of price support and formal credit
Rainfed farming with traditional seeds only
Assured irrigation, chemical fertilisers and institutional credit
n34dbd6d91f7.x: The package combined HYV seeds with assured irrigation, fertilisers, pesticides, mechanisation, institutional credit and MSP or assured procurement.

n83df54d9c76.s:
Consider the following statements about Operation Flood:
1. Phase I (1970-80) was financed by the World Food Programme.
2. Phase II (1981-85) raised milk sheds from 18 to 136.
3. The addition of 30,000 new dairy cooperatives came in Phase I.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n83df54d9c76.x: WFP financed Phase I and milk sheds rose from 18 to 136 in Phase II. The 30,000 new cooperatives came in Phase III (1985-96), not Phase I.

n6bb2405905c.s:
Consider the following statements about the costs of the Green Revolution:
1. Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana is estimated to be 35-57% more than recharge.
2. The predominant N:P:K fertiliser ratio was balanced at 1:1:1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n6bb2405905c.x: Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Haryana exceeds recharge by 35-57%. The N:P:K ratio was skewed at 10.9:4.1:1, not balanced at 1:1:1.

n0268e054e0c.s: Agricultural growth of only 0.73%, the lowest among the Plans, was recorded in the:
n0268e054e0c.x: The Third Plan recorded 0.73% agricultural growth; the Eighth Plan recorded 4.68% against a 4.1% target.

nce1612d136e.s: Which of the following pairs on India's global rank is correctly matched?
nce1612d136e.x: India ranks first in shrimp output and exports, but second in fish production and aquaculture.

new.s: The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
new.x: The scheme was launched at Suratgarh in Rajasthan on 19 February 2015.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Soil Health Card Scheme:
1. It is part of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (Soil Health Management).
2. The card gives soil nutrient status and fertiliser advice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The scheme falls under NMSA's Soil Health Management, and the card reports nutrient status with fertiliser advice.

new.s: Soil Health Cards are estimated to have cut fertiliser use by about:
new.x: Fertiliser use fell by 8-10% and yields rose by 5-6%.

new.s: Namo Drone Didi provides agricultural drones to:
new.x: Namo Drone Didi gives drones to women SHGs.

new.s: Under Namo Drone Didi, central assistance covers what share of drone cost, up to Rs 8 lakh?
new.x: The scheme gives 80% central assistance up to Rs 8 lakh.

new.s: The drone target of the Namo Drone Didi scheme (2023-24 to 2025-26) is:
new.x: It targets 15,000 drones with an outlay of Rs 1,261 crore.

new.s: Custom hiring centres and farm machinery banks are subsidised under:
new.x: SMAM (2014-15 to 2025-26) subsidises machines, custom hiring centres, hi-tech hubs and farm machinery banks.

new.s: Kisan Call Centres were launched on 21 January 2004 by the:
new.x: The Department of Agriculture launched Kisan Call Centres (1800-180-1551) in 2004.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Krishi Vigyan Kendras:
1. They are 100% funded by ICAR.
2. They are supervised through 11 ATARIs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: KVKs are fully ICAR-funded and work under 11 ATARIs.

new.s: ATMA, the demand-driven district extension society, was set up in:
new.x: ATMA dates from 2005; it plans through SREP.

new.s: The extension principle 'seeing is believing' is put into practice through:
new.x: 'Seeing is believing' is the principle behind demonstrations.

new.s: Under the Seed Village concept, farmers are given ____ to produce certified seed locally.
new.x: In a Seed Village, farmers receive foundation seed and produce certified seed locally.

new.s: The Varietal Replacement Rate is the share of area under varieties released in the last:
new.x: VRR measures area under varieties released in the last 3-5 years.

new.s: Genetically modified crops in India are approved by:
new.x: GEAC approves GM crops under the Rules of 1989 framed under the EPA 1986.

new.s: The Rules under which GEAC functions are framed under the:
new.x: GEAC works under the 1989 Rules of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, in MoEFCC.

new.s: GEAC cleared GM mustard DMH-11 in:
new.x: GEAC cleared DMH-11 in 2022; it is under Supreme Court scrutiny.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Seeds Act, 1966 – quality of notified seeds
PPV&FR Act, 2001 – ban on GURT (terminator) seeds
new.x: The Insecticides Act 1968 set up the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee; it has nothing to do with Seed Villages.

new.s: Genome-edited SDN-1 rice varieties fall outside GMO rules because they:
new.x: SDN-1 edits carry no foreign DNA, so DRR Dhan 100 Kamala and Pusa DST Rice 1 are outside GMO rules.

new.s: Endosulfan was banned in India in 2011 by the:
new.x: The Supreme Court banned endosulfan in 2011.

new.s: Neem-based products used in plant protection are classed as:
new.x: Neem-based products are bio-pesticides.

new.s: India still uses at least how many pesticides banned elsewhere?
new.x: India still uses at least 66 pesticides banned in other countries.

new.s: Under DBT in fertilisers, the subsidy is paid to:
o: fertiliser companies after sale at PoS devices
new.x: DBT pays the subsidy to companies after the sale is recorded on PoS devices, not to farmers.

new.s: How many grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers are covered under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme?
new.x: NBS (2010) covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about urea in India?
o: It is the most subsidised fertiliser
It remains under statutory price control
It gets a fixed per-kg subsidy under NBS
new.x: NBS covers P&K (and S); urea stays under statutory price control.

new.s: Neem coating became compulsory for imported urea from:
new.x: Neem coating was notified in May 2015, made compulsory for domestic urea from 1 Sep 2015 and for imported urea from 1 Dec 2015.

new.s: Nano DAP contains:
new.x: IFFCO's Nano DAP has 8% nitrogen and 16% phosphorus.

new.s: In world fertiliser production, India ranks:
new.x: India is the second largest consumer and third largest producer of fertilisers.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about organic inputs:
1. Vermicompost is made by earthworms turning organic waste into manure.
2. Bt cotton is a green manure crop.
3. Sunn hemp and dhaincha are green manure crops.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Vermicompost uses earthworms, and sunn hemp and dhaincha are green manures. Bt cotton is a GM crop, not a green manure.

new.s: Organic certification under NPOP (2001) is handled by:
new.x: NPOP is run by the Commerce Ministry through APEDA; PGS-India is a separate certification route.

new.s: The National Mission on Natural Farming was launched as a stand-alone mission in:
new.x: NMNF began as a stand-alone mission in November 2024.

new.s: 'Har Medh Par Ped' is the agroforestry component of:
new.x: NMSA's components are Rainfed Area Development, Soil Health Management and Agroforestry ('Har Medh Par Ped').

new.s: Which State has the largest tubewell-irrigated area?
new.x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest tubewell-irrigated area.

new.s: After December 2021, Per Drop More Crop has been implemented under:
new.x: Per Drop More Crop ran under PMKSY from 2015 to Dec 2021 and is now under RKVY.

new.s: Command Area Development and Water Management falls under which PMKSY component?
new.x: Har Khet Ko Pani covers CAD&WM, surface minor irrigation, repair of water bodies and groundwater.

new.s: The Central Tobacco Research Institute (CTRI) is located at:
new.x: CTRI is at Rajahmundry in Andhra Pradesh.

new.s: The National Rice Research Institute (formerly CRRI) is located at:
new.x: CRRI, now the National Rice Research Institute, is at Cuttack.

new.s: ICRISAT is located at:
new.x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru near Hyderabad.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Indian Institute of Maize Research – Hyderabad
new.x: The Indian Institute of Maize Research is at Ludhiana; the Hyderabad IIMR is for millets.

new.s: The World Bank-aided NAIP was implemented during:
new.x: NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014 with World Bank support; NATP began in 1998.

new.s: In 1966, how much Mexican wheat seed was imported and crossed with local varieties in Punjab?
new.x: India imported 18,000 t of Mexican wheat in 1966.

new.s: The Early Green Revolution phase covered the years:
new.x: Pre-Green Revolution was 1951-68, Early 1968-81 and Later 1987-92.

new.s: Norman Borlaug received the Nobel Peace Prize in:
new.x: Borlaug won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's fertiliser consumption in 2024-25 was about:
new.x: AP consumed 39.39 lakh MT of fertiliser in 2024-25.

new.s: After rationalisation, how many Rythu Seva Kendras remain functional in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Rythu Seva Kendras were rationalised from 10,778 to 8,489.

new.s: APCNF uses which bio-inputs?
new.x: APCNF relies on jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.

new.s: Which of the following is public investment (capital formation) in agriculture rather than an input subsidy?
new.x: PACS computerisation builds capital; power, fertiliser and credit subsidies are current transfers.

new.s: HYV seeds were first introduced in India in the Rabi season of:
new.x: HYV seeds came in the Rabi of 1966-67, during the Plan Holiday.

new.s: The Green Revolution began during the:
new.x: It began in the three Annual Plans of 1966-69 that followed the Third Plan.

new.s: C. Subramaniam, who led the Green Revolution policy push, received the Bharat Ratna in:
new.x: C. Subramaniam, Union Food and Agriculture Minister (1964-66), got the Bharat Ratna in 1998.

new.s: The Intensive Agricultural District Programme (1960) was piloted in how many districts?
new.x: IADP began in 7 districts of 7 States; IAAP later covered 114 districts.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about pre-Green Revolution programmes:
1. IADP (1960) began in 7 districts.
2. IAAP (1964-65) was extended to 114 districts.
3. IAAP in Andhra Pradesh began in East Godavari.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: IADP covered 7 districts and IAAP 114. In AP, IAAP began in West Godavari, not East Godavari.

new.s: The quicker maturity of HYV crops allows:
new.x: HYVs mature quicker, making double cropping possible.

new.s: The first semi-dwarf rice introduced in India (1965) was:
new.x: Taichung Native-1 came in 1965; IR-8 is the IRRI 'miracle rice' of 1966.

new.s: The rice variety called 'miracle rice' is:
new.x: IR-8, a dwarf rice from IRRI, Philippines, was called 'miracle rice'.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: TN-1 was India's first semi-dwarf rice; the IRRI 'miracle rice' was IR-8.

new.s: The BPT series of rice varieties comes from:
new.x: BPT = Bapatla; MTU = Maruteru.

new.s: Samba Mahsuri is the rice variety:
new.x: BPT 5204 (Samba Mahsuri) is a Bapatla variety and parent of DRR Dhan 100 Kamala.

new.s: India's first genome-edited rice, Pusa DST Rice 1, was developed from:
new.x: Pusa DST Rice 1 comes from MTU 1010, a Maruteru variety.

new.s: In the south, the rice gains of the Green Revolution came mainly in the:
new.x: Rice gains came in the Godavari-Krishna and TN deltas.

new.s: The early gains of the Green Revolution were concentrated in:
new.x: Punjab, Haryana and western UP gained most; the eastern rice states lagged.

new.s: Food self-sufficiency from the Green Revolution ended India's reliance on:
new.x: India stopped relying on PL-480 food imports.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an ecological cost of the Green Revolution?
new.x: N:P:K use became skewed at 10.9:4.1:1, not balanced; salinity, biodiversity loss and groundwater depletion were real costs.

new.s: Which crops were neglected by the Green Revolution?
new.x: Its crop bias neglected pulses, oilseeds and millets or coarse cereals.

new.s: In 2006, PM Manmohan Singh called for a Second Green Revolution at the 93rd Indian Science Congress held in:
new.x: The call came on 3 January 2006 at the 93rd Indian Science Congress in Hyderabad.

new.s: The concept of 'Evergreen Revolution' was given by:
new.x: Swaminathan's Evergreen Revolution means raising productivity in perpetuity without ecological harm.

new.s: The theme of the M.S. Swaminathan Centenary Conference (August 2025) was 'Evergreen Revolution, The Pathway to':
new.x: The theme was 'Evergreen Revolution, The Pathway to Biohappiness'.

new.s: How many States are covered under BGREI?
new.x: BGREI covers 7 States: Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Eastern UP and West Bengal.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a BGREI State?
new.x: Punjab is not covered; BGREI targets eastern rice States.

new.s: The White Revolution started in which State?
new.x: It started in Gujarat on the Amul model at Anand.

new.s: Who is known as the Father of the White Revolution?
new.x: Dr Verghese Kurien, who worked with Tribhuvandas Patel at Anand.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the White Revolution:
1. NDDB was set up in 1965 to copy the AMUL model.
2. Operation Flood was the world's largest dairy development programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: NDDB (1965) copied the AMUL model, and its Operation Flood (1970) was the world's largest dairy development programme.

new.s: White Revolution 2.0 aims to set up how many new dairy cooperative societies?
new.x: White Revolution 2.0 (Sept 2024) targets 75,000 new societies.

new.s: The Pink Revolution is associated with:
new.x: Pink covers meat processing, prawn, onion and pharmaceuticals (Durgesh Patel).

new.s: The Round Revolution relates to:
new.x: Round Revolution = potato, not oilseeds.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Fertilisers belong to the Grey Revolution; Brown is leather or cocoa.

new.s: The Blue Revolution is associated with:
new.x: Blue Revolution (fisheries) is linked with Hiralal Chaudhuri and Arun Krishnan.

new.s: Agriculture and allied growth was negative in which years?
new.x: 2002-03 and 2014-15 were negative; 2015-16 grew about 0.7%.

new.s: India's average agriculture and allied growth during FY16-FY25 was:
new.x: FY16-FY25 averaged 4.4%, the highest decadal growth, against a world average of 2.9%.

new.s: Provisional agriculture and allied growth for FY26 is:
new.x: FY26 is 3.0% (provisional); Q1 FY27 is 3.6%.

new.s: The highest agricultural growth among the Plans was recorded in the:
new.x: The Eighth Plan recorded 4.68%, the highest, against a 4.1% target.

new.s: India's foodgrain production in 1950-51 was about:
new.x: Foodgrains rose from 50.8 MT in 1950-51 to 211.9 MT in 2001-02.

new.s: India's foodgrain production in 2018-19 was about:
new.x: 2018-19 output was about 283 MT (3rd AE).

new.s: India's oilseed yield in 2024-25 was about:
new.x: Oilseed yield reached 1,398 kg/ha in 2024-25.

new.s: The NMEO target for oilseed production by 2030-31 is nearly:
new.x: NMEO aims at nearly 70 MT of oilseeds by 2030-31.

new.s: India ranks ____ in the world in wheat and sugarcane production.
new.x: India is 2nd in wheat, sugarcane, fruits, vegetables, eggs, cotton and silk.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's global rank:
1. As of January 2026, India is the largest producer of rice, ahead of China.
2. India is the largest producer of fruits and vegetables.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: India is now 1st in rice (150.18 MT vs China 145.28 MT). China is the largest producer of fruits and vegetables; India is 2nd.

new.s: In which of the following does India NOT rank first in the world?
new.x: India is 1st in milk, pulses and spices but 2nd in wheat.

new.s: The leading soybean-producing State is:
new.x: Madhya Pradesh leads in soybean, not Maharashtra.

new.s: The leading cashew-producing State is:
new.x: Maharashtra (~25%) leads, followed by Andhra Pradesh (~17%) and Odisha.

new.s: Which State was the leading rice producer in 2024-25?
new.x: The rice leader moved from West Bengal (2021-22) to Telangana (2023-24) to Uttar Pradesh (2024-25).

new.s: The leading rapeseed-mustard-producing State is:
new.x: Rajasthan leads in rapeseed-mustard.

new.s: Which State has the highest rice yield in India?
new.x: Punjab has the highest rice and wheat yields, thanks to canal and tubewell irrigation.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a State with below-national-average rice yield?
new.x: AP, Telangana and TN are above the national average; Odisha, UP and Bihar are below it.

new.s: India's average cotton yield is about:
new.x: India's cotton yield is about 440 kg/ha against a global ~770; Kapas Kanti targets 755.

new.s: About 67% of rice area is irrigated; the share for pulses is about:
new.x: Rice is ~67% irrigated against ~26% for pulses.

new.s: Post-harvest cold-chain losses in Indian agriculture are about:
new.x: Cold-chain losses are about 30%; lack of cold chains is a cause of the yield gap.

new.s: Which of the following drives total factor productivity growth in agriculture?
new.x: TFP is output growth beyond input growth; research, irrigation, roads, extension and education drive it.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about agricultural growth in India:
1. It has come more from area expansion than from yield.
2. Crop growth (3.5%) now leads livestock and fisheries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Growth comes more from area than yield. Statement 2 is wrong: livestock and fisheries now lead while crop growth lags at 3.5%.

new.s: Soybean area in Madhya Pradesh fell between 2023 and 2024 by about:
new.x: MP soybean area fell 10%; 37.5% is the fall in Punjab's cotton area.

new.s: Telangana's cultivated area grew from 1.31 crore acres (2014) to about ____ by FY23.
new.x: It rose to 2.2 crore acres via Kaleshwaram and Mission Kakatiya.

new.s: INSIMP, under RKVY, targets:
new.x: INSIMP (2011-12) is for millets.

new.s: In FY25 the National Food Security Mission was renamed:
new.x: NFSM became NFSNM in FY25.

new.s: The Doubling Farmers' Income Committee was chaired by:
new.x: Ashok Dalwai chaired it (set up 2016, report 2018), not Swaminathan.

new.s: The National Commission on Agriculture (1970) was chaired by:
new.x: NCA, set up in 1970, was chaired by N.R. Mirdha.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission on Agriculture:
1. It gave its final report in 1976 in 15 parts, including rural employment.
2. It was chaired by Ashok Dalwai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: NCA reported in 1976. It was chaired by N.R. Mirdha; Ashok Dalwai chaired the Doubling Farmers' Income Committee.

new.s: Which scheme addresses the eastern rice States left behind by the Green Revolution?
new.x: Eastern rice States lagged after the Green Revolution, hence BGREI.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Green Revolution outcomes:
1. It benefited wheat first, then rice.
2. It narrowed regional disparity among States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Wheat gained first, then rice. It widened, not narrowed, regional disparity.

new.s: The Green Revolution mainly benefited which regions?
new.x: Punjab, Haryana and western UP benefited; eastern rice States still lag.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's foodgrain production in 2025-26 (2nd AE) is:
new.x: AP's 2025-26 output is 190.29 lakh t, up 17.03%.
